name: Claude Monet
hook: The painter of light on water: haystacks, cathedrals, and the pond at Giverny.

facts.label: Impression, Sunrise
facts.statement: Impression, Sunrise (1872), a Le Havre port scene, gave Impressionism its name after critic Louis Leroy mocked it in 1874.

facts.label: Giverny
facts.statement: Monet settled at Giverny in 1883 and built the water-lily pond that inspired his late paintings; he died there in 1926.

facts.label: the Water Lilies
facts.statement: His Nymphéas series, exhibited in 1909, grew out of the pond at Giverny; the water lily is also a July birth flower.

facts.label: Rouen Cathedral
facts.statement: Monet painted Rouen Cathedral repeatedly, a series of views of the Gothic facade in changing light.

facts.label: the Thames
facts.statement: From 1899 to 1904 Monet painted the Thames and the Houses of Parliament in London.

facts.label: Camille Monet
facts.statement: Monet's wife Camille was a frequent model, notably in Woman with a Parasol.

facts.label: the rainbow palette
facts.statement: In the 1870s Monet introduced a "rainbow palette," banning black and brown from his work.
